neighbours.label: Game-description context: the function words right after a game is named or said to be played ('a game of…', 'the aim of the game is…', 'X is played…'); the same frames about a project, lesson or concert stay quiet.
fire: Backgammon is a game of luck and skill that two people play with dice.
In bowls, the aim of the game is to roll your ball nearest to the jack.
Dominoes is played with twenty-eight tiles laid end to end on a table.
Poker is a card game in which players bet on the strength of their hands.
The object of the game is to capture all of your opponent's pieces.
Hopscotch is a children's game played on a grid chalked on the pavement.
Bridge is a game for four players who sit in two partnerships.
In this board game, the first player to reach the last square wins.
quiet: Carpentry is a trade of patience and skill that two people can learn together.
In the workshop, the aim of the course is to build your own small bookshelf.
The sonata is performed with two violins seated side by side on a stage.
Pottery is a craft in which students shape the clay with their hands.
The object of the survey is to record all of the village's old wells.
The recipe is a family favourite cooked on a stove in the back kitchen.
The seminar is a class for four students who work in two pairs.
In this cooking class, the first student to finish the dish helps the others.

notes: Card: peaks on ' is', ' of', ' played' after 'game'; the pole's output promotes ' game'/' gameplay'. Probes: game frames 0.6-1.2, project/lesson frames under 0.1, puzzle 0.25.
